Subject: Redwood hosted API evaluation - quickstart & next steps

Hi Jordan -

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we have a clear evaluation plan:

- Scope: You mentioned wanting to validate the hosted API for the customer support summarization pipeline (short summaries, ~200 tokens output) and embeddings for semantic search on a 6-week pilot.
- Primary evaluation goals: latency under 200ms p50 for generation, stable cost per 1k tokens, and verifying that hosted data handling meets your security checklist (SOC2 + enterprise agreements).
- Deployment mode: For the pilot you indicated Hosted API was preferred for speed-to-value; Dedicated or Private are options later if you need sustained throughput or tighter network controls.

Immediate next steps I recommend:
1) I'll send a quickstart packet (attached) with sandbox API key, sample requests, and a pre-built evaluation notebook.
2) Aditya (cc) will share a small set of rate-limit and concurrency recommendations based on your expected traffic profile.
3) We'll schedule a 30-min check-in after your first 48 hours to capture any regressions and tuning.

Notes on hosted API for the evaluation:
- Base endpoint: https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate (see attached quickstart for full examples)
- Auth: Bearer API_KEY in Authorization header
- Suggested rate limits for pilot: 60 requests/minute for single-key sandboxes; we can raise this for dedicated trial keys if you need higher concurrency.
- Tokenization: we recommend batching short prompts up to 4 per request for cost savings; more aggressive batching is possible but may affect latency.

Attachments: Redwood-Hosted-API-Quickstart.pdf, evaluation-sample-requests.json

If that looks right, I'll provision a sandbox key and share the concise runbook for your engineering team.

Thanks,

Jordan - great questions. Short answers + actions below.

1) Burst/concurrency: The 60 req/min guidance is for our default sandbox (shared) keys to protect fairness. For pilot evaluation we can issue a dedicated sandbox key with higher soft limits - e.g., 1200 requests/minute with 50 concurrent connections - or enable short-term burst capacity. If you need sustained 150 QPS during business hours, we recommend a Dedicated trial pool (reserved capacity) which gives predictable throughput and SLA-backed latency; Aditya can run sizing quickly and propose a Dedicated trial if you want to test at production QPS.

2) Data handling statement: See attached excerpt (from the quickstart) - hosted sandbox does not persist customer prompt/response data to shared training or indexing stores by default; logs are retained for 30 days and can be configured per account. For enterprise customers we offer additional retention and audit controls and can sign the standard security addendum. If you want a short one-pager for your security team, I'll share one.

3) Move-up path: We typically do this progression: Hosted sandbox -> Hosted dedicated evaluation key (higher concurrency) -> Dedicated pool (reserved) or Private VPC. Each step includes an Ops checklist (rate limiting, connection pooling, token accounting). I've included a short checklist in the attached quickstart and linked the docs above.

Action items:
- I've attached the sandbox quickstart and sample requests (Redwood-Hosted-API-Quickstart.pdf, evaluation-sample-requests.json).
- Aditya, can you please send the preliminary rate-limit/concurrency recommendation and estimate for a Dedicated trial that can support 150 QPS? (cc'd)
- Jordan, I'll provision a dedicated sandbox key for tomorrow's run and post it into a secure HubSpot note (link below) - confirm which email you want it delivered to.

If it helps, we can do a 30-min runbook session with your infra lead before the test.

Thanks - speak soon.
